panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of Bloom syndrome patient face showing captioned malar telangiectasia, prominent nose, and dolicocephaly; article title is Bloom syndrome with lung involvement. Findings directly supported by caption and in-text mention.
panels.attribution_text: Nair et al. Bloom syndrome with lung involvement.. Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society 2009. doi:10.4103/0970-2113.53234. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Telangiectasia over cheeks and nose and prominent nose, dolicocephaly
in_text_mentions: He had short stature, height 117 cms, dolicocephaly, small face, bilateral malar telangiectasia, prominent nose, polydactyly were seen [Figure 1]. Secondary, sexual characters were present, absence of eyelashes bilaterally (madarosis), clubbing-Grade II present, cyanosis and tachypnoea with respiratory rate 35/min were present. Respiratory system revealed bilateral coarse crepitations and occasional wheeze.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of anterior abdominal skin from Bloom syndrome case report, caption and in-text explicitly attribute café au lait macules to Bloom syndrome patient; hyperpigmented macule visible with arrow annotation.
panels.attribution_text: Martinez et al. Adenocarcinoma of the Right Colon in a Patient with Bloom Syndrome.. Case reports in surgery 2016. doi:10.1155/2016/3176842. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Café au lait macules in the anterior abdominal skin.
in_text_mentions: ture (142 cm), weight of 48 kg, growth retardation, dolichocephaly, triangular face, beaked nose, prominent ears (Figure 2(a)), and hypogonadism. He had a high-pitched voice, small mandible, dystrophic nails, clinodactyly (Figure 2(b)), and palmar transverse crease (Figure 2(c)). He had a telangiectatic erythema in malar region of the face and forehead that worsened after solar radiation and a linear scar in brow related to previous surgical resection of a basal cell carcinoma (Figure 2(d)). He also presents with several café au lait macules in the abdominal skin and gluteal region (Figure 3).
